options.why: One basis point is 1/10000 of the notional; multiplying C cents by bps/10000 gives exact fee cents before rounding.
Dividing by 100 treats basis points as percent units and makes the fee 100 times too large.
The fee scales proportionally with bps; dividing by bps reverses that dependence and fails at zero.
This inverts the basis-point scale rather than applying bps/10000 to the notional cents.
